title: Localizing Data Annotation Faults in Semantic Segmentation Systems (SegFaultLoc)
mechanism: Training-free fault localisation: split masks into connected components, extract features from frozen pretrained encoders, build a semantic spectrum (class / missing faults) and a geometric spectrum (localisation / fragmentation faults), and rank components by learned suspiciousness.
adaptation: Rank train crack and inactive components across the 5 sources with DINOv2/DINOv3 features; check precision against the 24 cells the audit already flagged; set the top-ranked components to ignore or down-weight them (no hand labelling).
min_experiment: Arm: drop the top 5% of suspicious crack components (ignore index), retrain house, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: precision at 24 vs the audit list; test crack IoU and relF1@2. Kill: precision at 24 below 0.3, or crack IoU change under 0.012.
evidence: R: up to +9.2% APFD, +21.9% Precision@10%, +22.4% nDCG@10% over 7 data-quality baselines on 3 benchmarks; fixing faults it found in COCO-Stuff improved segmentation.
prior_overlap: none. The audit flagged 24 of 239 cells but nothing was fixed; automatic label refinement is listed as open.
